$sources: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.4.3, Eq 6.2.34 and the design spectrum for inelastic analysis (R = 1, I = 1) (part 1 pp. 612-613, gazette pp. 3193-3194)

sources.modelling: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.1 (p. 641-642): nonlinear force-deformation models of every element that yields, P-Delta, strengths not above the expected values, degradation
sources.controlPoint: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.1 (p. 642): control point at the centre of mass of the roof
sources.pattern: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.2 (p. 642): lateral forces at the centres of mass, proportional to the fundamental mode
sources.pushTo: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.2 (p. 642): continued to at least 150 % of the target displacement
sources.noDrop: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.2 (p. 642): no drop of the base shear up to 125 % of the target displacement
sources.bilinear: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.3 (p. 642): bilinear fit at 60 % of the effective yield strength, equal areas to the target displacement
sources.spectrum: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.4.3, Eq 6.2.34 with R = 1 and I = 1 (pp. 612-613)
sources.memberForces: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.4 (p. 643): member forces and deformations at the step the target displacement is reached
sources.acceptance: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.4 (p. 644): deformation at most 2/3 of that at loss of gravity support and of that at which the strength drops below 70 % of the peak
sources.review: BNBC 2020 Part 6 Sec 2.5.12.5 (p. 644): design review by an independent team

procedure.note: Sec 2.5.12.1 caps the element strengths at the expected values and gives no expected-strength factors: the fibre model uses the nominal strengths, which never exceed them.

targetDisplacement.note: Eq 6.2.54 prints Ts, which BNBC does not define; the condition above it names TC (Sec 2.5.4.3), so Ts is read as TC. Below Rd = 1 the structure stays elastic and Eq 6.2.54 has no meaning (it would give C1 < 1), so Rd is taken as at least 1 (C1 = 1): SAEngine practice, not BNBC.

acceptance.note: BNBC asks for the deformation capacities from laboratory test data and gives no strain values. The concrete limits come from the fibre model's own stress-strain curves (the strain where the confined core falls below 70 % of its peak). The bars and steel shapes do not lose strength in the fibre model, so a fracture or buckling strain of 0.06 is assumed for them (SAEngine practice, not BNBC; conservative against the uniform elongation of reinforcing and structural steel).
